description: VVC's Multiple Transform Selection (MTS) + Low-Frequency Non-Separable Transform (LFNST) decomposed. MTS lets the encoder pick from DCT-2, DST-7, DCT-8 per axis; LFNST applies a small non-separable secondary transform to the top-left low-frequency coefficients. Together they handle residual energy distributions the fixed DCT can't decorrelate well: ramped residuals (DST-7), flipped-ramp residuals (DCT-8), and diagonal/non-axis-aligned residuals (LFNST).

sub_mechanisms.name: DCT_2_basis
sub_mechanisms.definition: The classical DCT (basis: cos((2k+1)nπ/(2N))). Approximates the optimal KL transform for AR(1) signals with high correlation. The default transform.
sub_mechanisms.why: Optimal for residuals from many intra/inter prediction modes. The 'safe choice' that always works; MTS uses it when other transforms wouldn't help.

sub_mechanisms.name: DST_7_basis
sub_mechanisms.definition: Discrete Sine Transform type 7 (basis: sin((2k+1)(2n+1)π/(4N+2))). Has basis vectors that ramp from zero at one boundary toward maximum at the other.
sub_mechanisms.why: Intra-prediction residuals often ramp toward the boundary with the predictor (where prediction is best, residual is smallest). DST-7's ramped basis matches this shape — concentrating energy in fewer coefficients than DCT-2 would.

sub_mechanisms.name: DCT_8_basis
sub_mechanisms.definition: Discrete Cosine Transform type 8 (basis: cos((2k+1)(2n+1)π/(4N+2))). Mirror of DST-7: ramps toward the boundary opposite to where the predictor is.
sub_mechanisms.why: Some intra prediction modes (e.g., horizontal prediction with bottom-left reference) leave residuals ramping AWAY from the predictor. DCT-8 catches this flipped case. Together with DST-7 it covers the asymmetric residual family.

sub_mechanisms.name: per_axis_transform_selection
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each block independently picks a horizontal transform AND a vertical transform from {DCT-2, DST-7, DCT-8}. Signalled per block.
sub_mechanisms.why: Residual asymmetry can be in one axis but not the other (e.g., horizontal prediction asymmetric vertically but symmetric horizontally). Per-axis selection captures these mixed cases. 3x3 = 9 combinations, signalled in 2-4 bits.

sub_mechanisms.name: MTS_signal_skipping
sub_mechanisms.definition: MTS is signalled only when the block has more than a threshold number of non-zero coefficients. Small-residual blocks default to DCT-2.
sub_mechanisms.why: For tiny residuals, the few-coefficient gain from optimal MTS choice is dwarfed by the signalling cost. Skipping MTS for those blocks avoids unnecessary overhead.

sub_mechanisms.name: LFNST_top_left_4x4_or_8x8
sub_mechanisms.definition: LFNST applies a small (4x4 or 8x8) non-separable secondary transform to the top-left low-frequency coefficients after the primary MTS transform.
sub_mechanisms.why: Primary transforms are separable: row-pass then column-pass. They can't decorrelate residual structure that doesn't align with the axes (diagonal edges). LFNST is non-separable; its basis vectors can capture diagonal energy that separable transforms miss.

sub_mechanisms.name: LFNST_kernel_selection
sub_mechanisms.definition: LFNST has 4 kernel sets, each containing 2 kernels (8 total). The kernel set is derived from the intra prediction mode; the kernel index (0 or 1, or 'no LFNST' = 2) is signalled per block.
sub_mechanisms.why: Different intra modes leave different residual orientations. The kernel set is implicitly determined by the mode (no signalling cost); only the 1-bit kernel choice + LFNST-enable is signalled.

sub_mechanisms.name: LFNST_size_constraints
sub_mechanisms.definition: LFNST is only applied for blocks of size 4x4 to 32x32 with non-trivial residual. The kernel size is 4x4 for small blocks, 8x8 for larger ones (applied to the 8x8 top-left region).
sub_mechanisms.why: Larger LFNST kernels catch more residual structure but cost more compute. Block-size-adaptive kernel size matches the granularity of expected residual asymmetry — smaller block = smaller residual structure = smaller kernel.

sub_mechanisms.name: LFNST_after_MTS
sub_mechanisms.definition: LFNST runs AFTER the MTS-selected primary transform. The primary transform decorrelates as much as it can; LFNST cleans up the residual energy in the low-frequency corner.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cascaded transforms work best when the first does the gross decorrelation and the second handles the residue. MTS+LFNST in series gives a more complete decorrelation than either alone.

derivation_rules.name: transform_matches_residual_ramp_shape
if: intra prediction residual ramps toward the predictor
then: DST-7 outperforms DCT-2 on that axis
derivation_rules.why: DST-7's basis ramps in the same direction as the residual energy, concentrating it in fewer coefficients. Mathematically: DST-7 is the KL-optimal transform for residuals modeled as a half-sine ramp.

derivation_rules.name: non_separable_handles_diagonal_residual
if: residual energy is along a diagonal (not axis-aligned)
then: non-separable LFNST decorrelates it; separable primary transforms cannot
derivation_rules.why: Separable transforms are constrained to row-then-column or column-then-row operations; their basis vectors are axis-aligned tensor products. Diagonal residual energy requires basis vectors that span both axes simultaneously — exactly what non-separable transforms provide.

derivation_rules.name: per_axis_selection_handles_asymmetric_residuals
if: residual is asymmetric in horizontal but not vertical (or vice versa)
then: per-axis transform selection captures the asymmetry at low cost
derivation_rules.why: Forcing both axes to use the same transform would waste one axis. Per-axis selection has 9 combinations vs 3 for unified selection; the extra 4-2 bits of signalling are dwarfed by the residual savings.

derivation_rules.name: cascade_transforms_for_compound_residual
if: residual has multiple decorrelation structures (ramp + diagonal)
then: MTS then LFNST handle them in sequence
derivation_rules.why: Primary MTS catches ramp; LFNST catches diagonal residue. Each transform handles what the other can't, and the cascade exploits their orthogonality (LFNST's input is the MTS output, not the original residual).

derivation_rules.name: implicit_kernel_set_saves_signalling
if: residual orientation correlates with intra prediction mode
then: deriving the LFNST kernel set from intra mode saves explicit signalling
derivation_rules.why: Vertical intra prediction produces vertically-asymmetric residuals; horizontal prediction produces horizontally-asymmetric ones. Kernel set selection can be derived from this mapping; only the 1-bit choice within the set needs explicit signalling.
